v4.1.8

### Additions
- Added the Simple API (`AzSimple`), an optional beginner-friendly way to animate entities, items and block entities with one renderer class and no animator, controller or dispatcher. Model, texture and animation paths are found by name, idle/walk/death and custom `when` states play automatically, and `AzSimple.play`, `loop` and `stop` trigger animations from server or client code. Triggered animations support priorities, interrupt policies and holding the last frame, and extra layers support bone masks, additive blending, weights, fades and conditions.
- Added animation-authored pose modifier weights. An animation’s pose_weights sets or keyframes the pose layer weight of IK, look-at, spring and bone-limit modifiers for the animatable playing it, with fade in/out in ticks, and fades them back to their default weight when it stops. Requires AzureLib Animator 2.4.0.

### Fixes
- N/A

### Changes
- N/A

### Developer Notes
- Authored pose weights are applied by each AzAnimationController right after its state machine updates. Fixed weights use AzPoseLayer#fadeWeight once when the animation starts, so code can still change them; weight tracks call setWeight every frame while they play.

updates.changelog:
# Shiroi Visuals Rework

In this version, we've reworked several rendering systems to improve the overall visual quality, lighting accuracy, and atmosphere of the Overworld.

These changes include improvements to atmospheric rendering, shadow precision, color reproduction, and ambient bloom. We've also introduced a series of optimizations to reduce rendering overhead and improve overall performance.

Additionally, this update introduces **Vivid Lamps**, an optional advanced lighting system that allows light-emitting blocks to illuminate their surroundings and cast dynamic shadows in real time.

**Note:** Vivid Lamps can significantly increase GPU usage, particularly when multiple light sources are visible. For this reason, the feature is disabled by default.

![Jungle forest](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/dfa971b4c396f1cfee39dea97715843ad445f46a.png)

## Changelog:

### Looks

- Completely reworked atmospheric rendering to improve the overall appearance and consistency of the Overworld.
- Reworked environmental lighting for more vibrant and natural illumination.
- Improved shadow precision and consistency across different lighting conditions.
- Adjusted color reproduction for more accurate and balanced tones while preserving the original Vanilla appearance.
- Reworked ambient bloom to improve light diffusion and reduce excessive brightness around illuminated surfaces.

### New Features

**Vivid Lamps**

- Added an optional real-time lighting system for torches, lanterns, and other light-emitting blocks.
- Light sources can now illuminate nearby surfaces dynamically.
- Added support for dynamic shadows cast by supported light sources.
- Introduced multiple lighting modes to balance visual quality and performance.

![Vivid Lamps turn on!](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/c3e2a5abc1b4b23161b844353ff11ce94eccca91.png)

**Available Modes:**

- **OFF (Default):** Disables Vivid Lamps entirely.
- **BOOST:** Enables enhanced real-time lighting without dynamic shadows.
- **ON:** Enables real-time lighting with dynamic shadow casting.

### Improvements

- Refined lighting calculations to improve transitions between illuminated and unlit areas.
- Improved overall visual consistency between atmospheric lighting, shadows, and environmental colors.
- Adjusted bloom behavior to better integrate with the updated lighting system.

### Performance

- Introduced several rendering optimizations to reduce GPU overhead.
- Optimized various shader calculations to improve performance without compromising visual quality.
- Vivid Lamps remains disabled by default due to the additional rendering cost of dynamic lighting and shadow generation.

**Note:** Performance improvements may vary depending on hardware, resolution, and enabled graphical features. Vivid Lamps, particularly in ON mode, may have a significant performance impact in environments containing multiple light sources.

# Olaf's Relatively Placed Blocks 2.0.2

A patch for 2.0.1, for every supported version (1.20.1, 1.21.1, 1.21.5, 1.21.8, 1.21.10, 1.21.11, 26.1, 26.2 and 26.3). Thanks to everyone who sent reports and logs!

## Fixes
- **1.21.10 and 1.21.11: shared spaces now redraw at once.**
  - Placing a block into a shared space, or breaking one out of it, didn't show until another block was placed next to it. The client was told about the change but never asked to redraw the chunk. It is now, the same as on the other versions.

## New
- **A config file to keep specific blocks out:** `config/relativeblocks.json`, written on first launch.
  - `never_share` lists blocks that may never share a space, by relative placement or as a mixed slab. It is read again on `/reload`.
  - `no_orthostats` lists slabs that get no orthostat (vertical slab). It takes effect on the next game start.
  - Entries are block ids in four forms: one block (`minecraft:rail`), a whole mod (`somemod:*`), a pattern (`*:*_fence`), or, for `never_share` only, a block tag (`#minecraft:flowers`).
  - Everything not listed still works exactly as before; the lists only take blocks out. A bad entry is reported in the log and skipped, never a crash.

## Changes
- **Blocks that fill their space no longer share it.**
  - Some blocks have no collision box but still take up their whole block, and the mod was letting them share a space as if they were flowers. That is fixed for snow layers, fire, rails, cobwebs, powder snow, string (tripwire), frogspawn, redstone dust, nether portals, vines, glow lichen, sculk veins, resin clumps, kelp, big dripleaf, and two-block plants such as tall grass, large ferns, sunflowers, lilacs, rose bushes, peonies and pitcher plants. The 1.21.5+ bushes (bush, firefly bush) are included as well, since their hit box is the full block.
  - **Crops** (wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots, nether wart, torchflower and pitcher crops, pumpkin and melon stems, sweet berry bushes, cave vines, weeping and twisting vines, mangrove propagules) and **flowerbeds** (pink petals, wildflowers, leaf litter) no longer share either: they grow or spread to fill their own patch.
  - **Invisible technical blocks** such as the structure void are left alone.
  - All of this is decided by the block's shape and properties, not by a list of names, so other mods' blocks of the same kind behave the same way.
  - Still shareable as before: flowers, short grass, ferns, dead bushes, saplings, mushrooms, fungi, roots, sea pickles, seagrass, cactus flowers, torches, levers, buttons, bamboo, cocoa, flower pots, candles, lanterns, chains, end rods, lightning rods, fences, panes, bars, walls and gates.
- **For pack makers:** redstone dust has left the `relativeblocks:relative_placement_denied` tag, since the shape rule now covers it. Pressure plates and sugar cane remain in it.

## Good to know
- Blocks that stop sharing in this patch are only kept from being placed together from now on. Anything already sharing a space in your world stays as it is.
- Removing the mod from a world that already has orthostats or shared blocks in it shows a "Missing content" warning. Back up your world before removing any mod that adds blocks.

  button ([#60](https://github.com/fishstiz/packed_packs/issues/60)).
- Added descriptions to profiles, which are shown as tooltips on hover or
  focus ([#65](https://github.com/fishstiz/packed_packs/issues/65)).
    - Can be edited from the edit button on the profiles sidebar
- Added option to swap actions of the "Show Packs" button with the transfer sprite and quick transfer (double click)
  shortcut. ([#80](https://github.com/fishstiz/packed_packs/issues/80))
    - When on, the "Show Packs" button will instead transfer all packs within the folder, and the Select/Deselect button
      will open the folder. Double-clicking will now also open the folder instead of transferring all packs.
    - Can be toggled on, off, or for unlocked folders only
- Added option to configure the max width of the Packed Packs screen.
- Improved performance on resource loading when discovering folders, especially with deeply nested folders
  ([#82](https://github.com/fishstiz/packed_packs/issues/82)).
- Allowed root level packs to be added virtually to folders, same as with built-in packs. Same limitations also apply.
- Newly discovered sub folders will now be placed on top of the saved order.
    - **Note**: The order of packs (including subfolders) are saved within a folders config, allowing the order to be
      preserved when recursively transferring all packs of a folder. The sort option is also changed to "None" when
      entering a folder, which shows the preserved order instead of the previously selected sort option. This may
      explain some confusion regarding why sub folders may show below regular packs.
- Opening dropdowns now change the focus to the dropdown container, which may work around some issues with mods that
  attempt to fix [MC-259387](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC/issues/MC-259387) by resetting the focus of buttons on
  click ([#79](https://github.com/fishstiz/packed_packs/issues/79)).
    - **Note**: This does not fix all compat issues with mods that do this, and I do not agree with the attempted fixes
      since it breaks focus. Mojang's changes (or possibly fix) to the issue in 26.4 snapshot 7 is more preferable.

updates.changelog:
## [2.17.5] - 11/15/2026
### Fixed
- Bank styles that list the mod's log stumps or straight fallen logs now place them; on level ground they never appeared.
- With Flashback on Fabric, replays recorded on a server no longer show other mods' blocks as the wrong block, such as Terrain Slabs' grass slabs as farmland.

## [2.17.4] - 11/14/2026
### Changed
- With Particular 1.6.0 or newer, waterfall foam at streams is three times bigger.

### Fixed
- With Particular installed, waterfall foam no longer piles up endlessly on streams.

## [2.17.3] - 11/13/2026
### Added
- A `streamDimensions` setting picks which dimensions get streams and lakes; it starts as just the Overworld.
- A `wands` setting turns the Flow and Carve Wands off for a whole pack.
- Bank style fields: `steepness` swaps blocks on steep ground, `wander_across` and `wander_along` set how the edges wander, `shore_reach` sets how far a lake shore's bank reaches, and `claims_banks` lets a style dress the land beside world-generated rivers and oceans.

### Changed
- Banks reach further back from the water, with a wider waterline, and end in a ragged, patchy edge where the land's own ground takes over.
- Most biomes' banks mix in patches of other ground blocks and turn rocky on steep ground.
- Lake shore banks step in and out along the shore, reaching further around a big lake than a pond.
- Bank style files give each ring a single reach, out from the water plus up; older files still load.
- A stream's current runs exactly as wide as its water.
- Waterfalls spray out to your render distance, however many are in view and with Subtle Effects too, from the moment their land loads; falls you've seen are remembered between sessions.
- Streams are prepared much faster on most FreeTerraForged worlds.
- Still Life: its rivers keep the banks Still Life drew, mediterranean banks get a cobblestone and terracotta waterline, and streams through its beaches keep the beach's own ground.

### Fixed
- Generating the End and the Nether no longer stalls the server.
- River currents you've seen keep their direction for good, through setting changes, updates and exploring, unless you change them yourself.
- In land you've reflowed, rivers no longer flow the wrong way for a moment when you arrive.
- Waterfall spray no longer vanishes when you walk up close to a fall.
- Waterfalls taller than 16 blocks now spray at their foot, with bigger foam for taller falls.
- Streams near a river no longer pick up its current and flow backwards.
- A stream flowing into a river swings round into the river's current instead of running across or against it.
- Lakes look still: water only flows near where streams run in or out.
- In rivers that don't flow (river currents turned off), a stream's current fades out a short way in, as in a lake.
- A stream through a lake above sea level no longer has a strip of still water between its flowing stretches.
- Streams spill down their small steps instead of leaving the water above a step as a still ledge. New land.
- Streams stop a few blocks past the shore of the sea or a lake instead of running on tens of blocks into the water. New land.
- With Flowing Fluids, waterloggable blocks placed in a stream come out waterlogged.
- Lake shores at water level wear the same bank material all the way round.
- With Particular installed, streams no longer fill the screen with endless waterfall foam.

## [2.17.1] - 11/6/2026
### Fixed
- With Caves Reflowing, a stream that starts where water from underground comes back out is as wide as the stream that went under, and the water below it widens to match, instead of starting as a thin trickle. New land.

## [2.17.0] - 11/6/2026
### Added
- Carve Wand (two sticks over a Heart of the Sea): lay out a stream like the Flow Wand, set its width and height at each point, and click the air to carve it as a real stream, with the same banks, berms and shore materials and a current running along it, its water three blocks under each point. A path starts a block wide and widens half a block with each point you add. Sneak-click the air to reverse its flow, or hold it to clear every path not yet carved. Points can be raised or lowered freely, so a stream can run uphill. Carving again after an edit, or removing the path, puts the old ground back.
- With Caves Reflowing, water from a stream that goes underground can come back out lower down as a new stream that runs on to a river, lake or the sea and swells the water below it. New land.
### Changed
- The Flow Wand is crafted from two sticks over a nautilus shell.
- Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac) while holding a Flow or Carve Wand undoes your last wand action, including any ground it dug or put back.
- Flow and Carve Wand points sit level with the top of the block they were placed on, their curve handles always stand out ready to grab, and the path you are editing stays drawn however far it runs.
- Default stream banks sit tighter to the water and fade softly into the land in patches, with no wide banks ending in a hard line.
- Bank styles can set `blob_size` to give patches a fixed size in blocks.
- Stone, gravel and other shore materials now stay right at the waterline, with only rare patches higher up; the rest of each bank matches the surrounding ground. Taiga banks no longer turn to cobblestone far up the slope.
- Shore materials reach at most 10% of a stream's width out from the water by default; a bank style's waterline can set `reach` to change that.
- Lake and sea shores wear their shore materials in a band as narrow as a 12-block-wide stream's, instead of a much wider one.
- Half of each waterfall's spray is now thick, chunky froth that stays close to the foot of the fall.
- Streams no longer end in lakes too small to hold them; a lake must be at least four times as wide as the stream that flows into it. New land.

## [2.16.2] - 10/27/2026
This Release includes all changes between 2.16.0 - 2.16.2
### Highlights
- **Streams 3x as fast!** Stream planning moves 3x as fast. Existing worlds keep their streams exactly as they were.
- **Half the CPU, just as many streams** Stream planning uses about half the CPU on heavy terrain packs. Existing worlds keep their streams exactly as they were.
- **Reflow the world you already have.** `/streams reflow` gives every pond, stream and channel in an existing world a current that runs downhill to the sea, and `/streams reflow carve` cuts new streams into land generated without the mod, with a preview first and an exact undo. Built areas and villages are left alone.
- **The Flow Wand.** Draw currents by hand like a pen tool: click to place points, drag to bend the curve and set how wide and deep it runs. Sneak-click the air for still mode, which calms a patch or a strip of water. Players without the mod can use it too.
- **No more structure freezes.** Nether portals, trial-chamber vaults, `/locate`, explorer maps and eyes of ender no longer freeze the game for minutes while a structure in fresh land waits for its streams.
- **Works on more worlds.** Streams and waterfalls now generate on worlds whose floor is below y=-64 (Tectonic `min_y` -128 or -512), and rivers from datapacks and mods such as Geophilic flow and take in streams like vanilla rivers.
- **Tidier banks, water and ice.** Banks stand a block above the water near every drop, streams no longer spill into caves or drain through sand and gravel, and ice at a freezing line ends in ragged edges instead of square patches.
- **Simplified Chinese and Subtle Effects.** The settings screen is now available in Simplified Chinese, and Subtle Effects' waterfall foam, splashes and drips work with this mod's streams and waterfalls.

## [2.16.2]
### Added
- The Flow Wand has a still mode (sneak-click the air): a single point makes a round patch of calm water you can widen, and a drawn path makes a calm strip.
- The settings screen is now available in Simplified Chinese.

### Changed
- Stream planning uses about half the CPU on heavy terrain packs, and new land generates sooner as you explore. The streams are exactly the same as before.
- New worlds plan streams faster again on every terrain accuracy level below Extreme. Worlds you already have keep their streams exactly as they were.
- With Horizons Reshowing installed, new worlds on Medium place streams from a finer reading of the ground.
- Streams no longer spill where they cut through a cave under the bank.
- Sand and gravel beside stream water no longer drop into caves below and drain the stream.
- With TerraFirmaCraft, streams can end in its rivers and oceans.
- A stream's built-up banks always stand at least one block above its water, so they hold it in.
- With Subtle Effects installed, its waterfall foam now shows at the foot of this mod's waterfalls instead of along every small step of a stream, under the same waterfall foam settings as Effective and Particular.
- With Subtle Effects installed, its splashes, drips, bubbles and melting snow now work in stream water as they do in any other water.

### Fixed
- Where a stream or lake crosses from freezing land into warmer land, its ice no longer ends in square 4-block patches and dead-straight lines beside open water; the edge of the ice is as ragged as on the world's own rivers. New land.
- Rivers from datapacks and mods such as Geophilic now flow and take in streams like vanilla rivers, where before their current stopped at the border with any other river and most streams around them were missing. New land.
- Map mods and other screens now show the stream biome's name instead of a raw key.
- On Fabric, block and fluid tooltips such as Jade's now call stream water "Water" instead of showing a raw key.
- On a new install, no stream starts and no lake forms in Terrestria's caldera and canyon biomes again; a config file you already have keeps its own biome blacklist.
- Nether portals, trial-chamber vaults, `/locate`, explorer maps and eyes of ender no longer freeze the game for minutes in freshly generating land while a structure there waits for its streams; that structure is placed straight away instead.
- Streams and waterfalls now generate on worlds whose bottom is lowered below y=-64 (for example Tectonic with `min_y` set to -128 or -512), which until now got few or none. New land.

## [2.16.1] - 10/24/2026

Everything in 2.16.0, plus the changes below.

### Added
- `/streams reflow carve radius <blocks>` carves new streams into land that was generated without the mod, following the ground that is actually there; places players have lived in and villages are left alone, and `/streams reflow carve undo` puts the land back exactly. `carve preview` shows the plan first without changing anything.
- The Flow Wand (`/streams wand`, the Tools & Utilities creative tab, or crafted from two sticks above a Heart of the Sea) draws currents by hand, like a pen tool: click water to place points, drag to bend the curve, and drag the red and green arrows to set how wide and how deep the current runs. Players without the mod can use it too, within arm's reach.

### Changed
- A stream's banks now always stand a block above its water within 7 blocks of any step down in the stream, so water no longer slops over the bank at small drops. New land.
- Near where a stream ends -- its last 4 blocks of height above the sea, lake or river it flows into -- its banks stay level with the water, with no raised rim along beaches and shores. New land.
- On Fabric, currents no longer go missing after leaving a world and opening it again without restarting the game.
- The mod no longer writes `streamsreflowing-stall-...txt` files beside your world when chunk generation pauses; they were a diagnostic, and most were false alarms.

## [2.16.0] - 10/16/2026

Everything in 2.15.2, plus the changes below.

### Added
- `/streams reflow radius <blocks>` (or `all`) gives the water already in a world a current that runs downhill: ponds drain through every exit, streams flow into each other and on to the sea, lakes or lagoons, and water with nowhere lower to go stays still. For worlds made before the mod, WorldPainter maps and hand-dug channels. `/streams reflow clear radius <blocks>` (or `clear all`) removes it.

## [2.15.2] - 10/14/2026

Everything in 2.15.1, plus the changes and fixes below.

### Changed
- On a multiplayer server, the settings screen now says that changes made there do not change the server, and stars the settings that the server's own settings file decides.
- Streams follow UltraTerraForged's terrain and rivers the way they follow ReTerraForged's; its own rivers keep their still water. New land.

### Fixed
- With One Dimension installed, streams no longer line their beds and banks with netherrack or end stone, and no longer cut channels and holes into the Nether and End layers of the world. New land.
- On FreeTerraForged worlds that also have Lithosphere or Still Life installed, streams no longer sit above the ground on raised banks in newly created worlds.
- FreeTerraForged rivers: the water's current and the drifting particles now run the same way, downstream and along the river's bends; on some rivers the particles drifted upstream.

## [2.15.1] - 10/11/2026

Everything in 2.15.0, plus the changes and fixes below.

### Changed
- Villages and other structures built from many pieces can now stand across streams and lakes: only the buildings that would sit in the water are left out. New land.
- Village paths cross streams on small bridges: a deck of the village's own planks on log posts. New land.
- A stream running along a hillside or cliff now gets a raised bank on its downhill side, so it no longer spills off the edge. New land.
- The built-up bank of a stream over a drop is rounder: its outer edge steps down and its underside slopes in under the water, where it used to end in a square ledge. New land.

### Fixed
- The minimum stream length now applies to a whole stream with all its branches: a branching stream whose longest arm is shorter than the minimum is removed, where before only unbranched streams were. New land.
- With Flowing Fluids installed, streams are protected from being drained by it again, and the error this left in the log when a world loads is gone.

## [2.15.0] - 10/9/2026

### Highlights
- **MC 26.3 Support** Users may encounter bugs, please report them to our discord if so.
- **One settings screen everywhere.** The same screen on Fabric, NeoForge and Forge, on every Minecraft version, with presets, search and plain names.
- **Presets.** Seven one-click setups from "Small scale, light" to "Massive scale, overnight pregen".
- **Players can help the server.** Players with the mod can plan streams for the land they explore, so the server does less.
- **Better waterfalls.** Spray that jumps and falls back, bigger foam on taller falls, and a choice of Effective's and Particular's foam.
- **Currents you can tune.** Separate sliders for how hard water pushes players, boats and mobs.

### Added
- A settings screen with tabs, sliders, search, a reset button per setting, a performance-cost colour beside each setting, and changes that save on their own. Forge 1.20.1 had no screen before.
- Seven presets that set the stream system size, terrain accuracy, shortest stream and smallest lake together.
- A 256-block stream system size.
- Sliders for how hard flowing water pushes players, boats and mobs, from none to four times the game's own push.
- With Effective or Particular installed: a switch to show their waterfall foam at this mod's waterfalls, and a choice of whose foam shows (none, theirs, this mod's, or both).
- Multiplayer: the server setting "Players help prepare streams" lets the games of players who have this mod plan streams for the server. Off by default; helpers are sent the world seed.
- A setting to turn off terrain estimates and read every land height in full.

### Changed
- NeoForge and Forge now use the same settings files as Fabric, `streamsreflowing.properties` and `streamsreflowing-client.properties`. Existing settings are carried over on first start and the old `.toml` files are kept with `.imported` added.
- Boats are pushed twice as hard by flowing water, and players and mobs a fifth harder. This applies to all flowing water.
- Waterfall spray jumps up and drops back, and taller waterfalls throw larger puffs. The smallest puffs are a quarter smaller than before.
- "Amount of water" at 100% now gives what 80% gave before. Affects land not yet generated, in existing worlds too.
- New defaults, for new settings files only: shortest stream 75 blocks (was 50), smallest lake about 32 blocks across (was about 23), driest climates keep a tenth of the usual water (was a fiftieth), and streams no longer end in biomes tagged only as "wet".
- Fabric gains the "ragged bank edges" setting.
- Removed the "older stream fluid" setting for Fabric dedicated servers; "Always use stream water" covers the same need.

### Fixed
- In worlds built with Lithostitched (Regions Unexplored, many Terralith and Tectonic packs), streams and lakes take the pack's own river biome instead of plain vanilla river. New land.
- World generation is no longer held up for minutes by a structure waiting on nearby streams, and the log says when generation is waiting on stream planning.

## [2.14.6] - 10/8/2026

### Fixed
- Grass, flowers and ferns are no longer left hanging in the air around a lake whose shore was cut back into a slope. New land.
- A tree is no longer left hanging in the air where a stream bank or lake shore was cut out from under it; it is removed, leaves and all. New land.

## [2.14.5] - 10/5/2026

### Performance
- 23% faster stream planning on MC 26.3

### Changed
- A blacklisted biome no longer cuts a stream off at its border: no stream starts there and no lake forms there on its own, and a stream that starts elsewhere runs through. New worlds; existing worlds keep the old behaviour.
- The biome blacklist is empty on a new install; it used to list three volcanic biomes from Terralith, Terrestria and Oh The Biomes We've Gone. An existing config keeps its list.
- The smallest lake is now about 512 blocks of water surface by default, down from 1024, so small lakes form more often. New land; a config file you already have keeps its own value.
- On Minecraft 26.3, streams and lakes on POTATO, LOW and MEDIUM read the land at spots where it is cheapest to read, cutting the terrain reading a watershed needs by about an eighth, and those lakes get finer shorelines. New setting `alignReadPoints` (on) turns it off to place every point exactly.

### Fixed
- A basin that only just met the smallest-lake size no longer fills as a lake of a single cell-wide patch of water. A pool in the path of a stream still fills whatever its size. New land.
- With a datapack or mod that changes whether rivers freeze, streams no longer show broken lines of open water or ice along chunk borders: a stream now freezes exactly as that world's rivers do. New land.
- The NeoForge 26.3 download loads again on current NeoForge builds; it now needs NeoForge 26.3.0.48 or newer, and says so instead of crashing on older ones.
- On NeoForge for Minecraft 26.1 and 26.2, streams now spawn the mobs other mods add to rivers, as they do on every other version.

## [2.14.4] - 10/3/2026

Everything in 2.14.3, plus the fixes below.

### Changed
- Lake shorelines are much rounder, especially on the lower terrain-accuracy levels, where they showed blocky corners and notches. Small ponds keep their shape. Applies to new lakes; lakes already in a world keep their shoreline.

### Fixed
- With the water source conversion gamerule on, diagonal waterfalls keep their shape instead of filling in to solid cubes of still water. New water sources now only form where the water is closed in on all four sides, so pools and trenches still refill.
- The game no longer refuses to start when another mod, or a Minecraft change, leaves one of this mod's hooks with nothing to attach to; that one feature is skipped instead. This covers the crash without Sodium installed.
- The game no longer fails to start without a shader mod installed when mixin checks are strict (seen alongside C2ME).
- The NeoForge 1.21.1 and 1.21.11 downloads no longer install on other Minecraft versions, where they crashed at startup; NeoForge now names the version you need instead.

## [2.14.3] - 9/28/2026

Corrections, plus Minecraft 26.3 as an early preview. On newly generated land, stream widths and lake levels can differ from 2.14.1 -- both from fixes below.

### Added
- Minecraft 26.3 on Fabric and NeoForge, as an EARLY PREVIEW: it loads and generates, but without the terrain work 26.3 needs, so treat those worlds as throwaway. 26.1 and 26.2 are unchanged.
- A mod logo, so the mod shows one in the mods list.
- Setting "physicsModWater": 3 (default) keeps this mod's moving water and keeps the Physics Mod's ocean off streams, 1 hands stream surfaces to that ocean instead, 0 leaves that mod alone.

### Changed
- With the Physics Mod installed, streams are filled with this mod's own water so that mod's ocean leaves them alone. Applies to new land.
- This mod no longer changes any of the Physics Mod's settings. If its ocean physics is off in its own menu, turn it back on once.

### Performance
- Rain near rivers no longer drops the frame rate. In singleplayer it could fall to single digits beside streams while raining.
- Waterfall spray costs far less to draw.
- Distant falls behind you no longer build up spray. Turn back and it fills in within a second.
- Large Sable vessels (Create Aeronautics and similar) cost far less server time, including ones nowhere near water.
- Less spray while it rains. Clear weather is unchanged.

### Fixed
- An intermittent crash at launch with C2ME installed, which struck on some launches and not others.
- A stream is now as wide as the streams that reach it, instead of standing at river width a few blocks below its source. New land.
- Still-looking patches along an otherwise moving stream.
- A lake settles at one level instead of a high rim around a lower middle. New land; a lake that already exists keeps its level.
- The middle of a large lake wears bed material instead of the grass the land grew.
- A lake over a cave no longer stands on nothing: its bed closes underneath with tapered rock. New land.
- Streams no longer stop dead at a mineshaft entrance, and a mineshaft whose tunnels reach a distant stream is no longer dropped from the world. New land.
- Streams no longer end in empty ground above a buried structure. New land.
- Buildings no longer stand on a stream crossing their grounds. New land.
- Bank materials no longer change along a chunk border. New land.
- Trees beside a stream keep their trunks, so no canopy hangs unsupported over the water.
- With Dynamic Trees, trees no longer grow inside lakes. New land.
- Water falling down a drop keeps moving from the lip to the pool.
- Frost walker lays ice on stream water, and that ice thaws back to stream water instead of a plain patch that Flowing Fluids can drain away.
- Rivers and oceans no longer freeze over in warm biomes. New land only: an existing world is not repaired.
- Streams and lakes no longer take their weather from a dimension another mod adds.
- Stream water and ordinary water no longer turn into each other where they meet.
- Elaina's Broom, and any entity a pack tags, is no longer swept away by a current.
- A fish or item you reel in reaches you instead of drifting off. Loose items still drift downstream.
- With Flowing Fluids, streams no longer swell, climb or spill out sideways. On Fabric they had no protection at all.
- Streams follow ReTerraForged and FreeTerraForged terrain, and those mods' rivers get a current. This had never worked in a published build, and is not yet verified in game.
- Particular's and Effective's waterfall effects stand down along streams; neither compatibility had ever taken effect. 26.x NeoForge gets them too.
- Waterfall foam from Particular or Effective keeps to a limit instead of building up without one.
- Video Settings / Particles now quietens waterfall spray, a particle limit of zero stops every particle, and the limit holds for one waterfall as well as for all of them.
- With Sodium, a stream meets a lake or the sea flush instead of showing a seam.
- A rare crash while chunks arrived around a stream.
- The spill-over-water setting now warns that turning it off can overflow other mods' water tanks and channels.

## [2.14.1] - 9/20/2026

### Added
- A bank style's `bed` and `waterline` rings can now plant scenery in the water itself: `bed` on the submerged floor (sea grass, kelp, coral) and `waterline` at the open surface (lily pads), alongside the existing land placements on `bank` and other rings.

### Changed
- Bank styles are rings out from the water: bed, waterline, bank, an optional second bank ring, and more, and every size is a percentage of the stream's width, so a wide river wears wide banks and a brook narrow ones from the same file. Lists of blocks mix as patches instead of a per-column speckle, rings blend more softly into each other, a style can swap its blocks where a stream is steep, fast, bending, near its mouth or on a long flat, and can put scenery on a ring. A starred style wins over the other styles of its kind; beaches are starred by default. Styles written for earlier versions keep working unchanged. See GUIDE.md in the bank_styles config folder.
- The built-in bank styles show their mixed materials as patches instead of a block-by-block scatter: river and forest beds come as stretches of gravel and stretches of clay, taiga shallows as cobble and gravel, and the sand on the inside of a bend reads as a bar rather than flecks. Applies to new land.
- A bank feature file with no biomes or tags is a definition now, placed where a style's ring names it; a file that names biomes or tags places itself as before. Leftover files naming scenery the mod withdrew are removed on load.
- The guide and examples in the bank config folders are rewritten for the new format, and refresh themselves whenever the format changes.
- The bank styles `examples/` folder is a set of worked examples now -- one per technique, each explaining itself, with `08_everything.json` using every field the format has: all eight stream properties, all three material patterns, and scenery on the bed, at the waterline and on the banks. The copy of all 47 shipped styles it used to hold is gone (a style you write replaces the shipped one for the biomes it names, so you never needed the file), and the examples sit in `examples/` itself rather than a `techniques` subfolder. Two more ready-made scenery definitions are seeded: lily pads for a waterline ring and seagrass for a bed ring.
- Streams sit in their valleys and follow the ground along their whole length on every terrain-accuracy setting, POTATO included. New setting, "terrain fit": closest, lighter, or none; follows the terrain-accuracy setting by default.
- Lake shorelines now follow the terrain-accuracy setting too: finer on EXTREME and MAX, unchanged on HIGH, and a little coarser but quicker to generate on MEDIUM, LOW and POTATO. Applies to new land only.
- MAX routes streams on a finer grid than before.
- HIGH, EXTREME and MAX no longer cover the land in tiny headwater streams: a stream needs the same amount of land draining into it on every accuracy level, so a higher level places the same streams more closely instead of adding many more. Applies to new land.
- Streams follow valleys and ridges more closely in rugged terrain: the land is now read in full wherever it bends, instead of being estimated between readings. New setting, "adaptive grid read", on by default; turning it off plans streams faster. Applies to new worlds.
- Streams no longer loop back on themselves or leave nubs on their banks: where a stream bends back close enough to touch itself, it cuts straight across, the way a river cuts off an oxbow. Applies to new land.
- A stream that runs into a pit too deep to cross and too small to be a lake now fills it as a plunge pool and carries on from the rim, instead of ending there. Mostly seen on HIGH and above, which are the levels that notice such pits. Applies to new land.
- New setting, "legacy stream shaping": places streams the way 2.13.x did, for comparing the two or for keeping new land in step with a world begun on an earlier version.
- The config is reorganised around what you are looking for: performance and stream planning first (the accuracy level, the watershed size, how far rivers are planned), then stream appearance, water behaviour, and particles and sounds, each in its own section, with short descriptions that fit the in-game tooltips. Watershed size is now a plain choice of 512 to 8192 blocks (1024 by default) instead of following the accuracy level. Settings you had are carried over, and a world keeps the watershed size it was started with whatever the setting says later, so existing worlds are unaffected.
- Rivers and waterfalls underground (the Caves Reflowing addon) are heard when you are down there with them, and cave waterfalls spray. Water beneath the ground you stand on stays silent: a river or fall below you is heard through open air but not through a floor of rock, while a wall beside you never blocks it.
- Bank plant life, flora and bank materials on all water, underwater plants and floating-snow cleanup no longer follow the terrain-accuracy setting: each is its own setting, on at the level MEDIUM had, on every accuracy level, and floating-snow cleanup simply always runs. POTATO and LOW worlds gain them.

### Fixed
- A lake dug into a hillside no longer leaves a flat wall of dirt standing over its water: its shore is now shaped the way a stream's banks are, sloping gently up out of the water and easing into the surrounding land, whether that land stands four blocks above the lake or forty. Applies to new land.
- A lake now shallows as it reaches its shore instead of holding its full depth to the water's edge, so you wade out of it up a beach rather than stepping off a ledge. Applies to new land.
- A lake shore cut into a hillside wears the ground the land around it wears -- turf over its own soil -- instead of showing bare rock where the cut went in. Applies to new land.
- Streams now meet a lake at its real shoreline: they are held at its surface, pour into it and leave it by the water's own edge, rather than by a blockier outline that could sit a few blocks off it. Applies to new land.
- Lake shorelines curve between one stretch of shore and the next, instead of running as straight facets meeting at angles. Applies to new land.
- On NeoForge and Forge, streams no longer leave whole chunks uncarved where a biome mod's biomes are not listed as overworld biomes (Still Life among them); they now form in every biome the overworld generates, as on Fabric.
- The POTATO terrain-accuracy setting now generates new land as quickly as intended; its streams may sit slightly differently than before.
- A lake whose outlet leaves over a waterfall is no longer removed, which left a river starting at full width from nowhere and the streams that fed the lake missing.
- Streams meeting at a confluence are no longer removed as dead ends when the river carries on from that very spot, which left the river below suddenly wider with nothing joining it; many more tributaries survive, most noticeably on EXTREME and MAX.
- Streams no longer stop on dry ground short of the sea where the flats along the shore count as ocean (World Reflowing's coasts, for one); they now run on into the water, in newly generated land.
- Rare "Detected unsafe terrain read" warnings in server logs on wide streams, from a bank column's waterfall check reaching across chunk borders. It now stays within the safe range, like the rest of the carve.
- River currents that reach the sea no longer sometimes flow backward, toward the land instead of out to the coast; most noticeable with biome mods that reshape the coastline.
- The shortest-stream setting now catches a tiny stream that joins another one right before the coast, not just a lone stream running straight to the sea; previously that case was always kept regardless of the setting.
- On Minecraft 26.x, items, mobs and boats drift at the stream's own speed again instead of one fixed rate, and water mobs set to hold position in a current (drowned included) no longer get swept along.
- `riverDrainageSize`'s description now states its true default (one watershed), replacing a stale claim of twice that no longer matched the setting's real behaviour.

# Punchy v3.2b

A hotfix for 3.2a.

## Fixes

- Your hand no longer flickers, or turns into Minecraft's hand, while you hold foods or blocks that a mod gives a quality or changes the food value of, such as with Kaleidoscope Cookery or Quality Food. The item no longer shakes either.
- Item physics keep their own settings after you save a pose in the Hand Editor, so a lantern no longer swings wildly once a profile is saved.
- With Spatial GUI, your hand now moves in the inventory when your main hand is set to Left, too.
- With Essential, an outfit that covers your arms now shows its sleeves and gloves on Punchy's arms, instead of leaving your hands invisible and your item floating.
- An item that a mod lets you charge and throw like a trident, such as an axe with ReArm's Crippling Throw, now charges and throws like a trident, instead of looping its use animation or holding it like a spear.
- With Flashback, spectating a player in a replay now shows Punchy's arms and first-person animations instead of Minecraft's, on every version Flashback supports. Mining, inspecting and keybind animations aren't in replays yet.
- While Create's netherite backtank is worn, an arm that a mod hides or gives another look now stays hidden or keeps that look.
- The first-anniversary celebration is over: the birthday cake and gift are held like any other item again.

## For pack creators

- `use_trident` and `use_trident_throw` now play for any item a mod lets you charge and throw like a trident. Give the item its own `use_trident` and `use_trident_throw` entries to animate it your way.
- The built-in pack has `spatial_compat_animation_left`, the left-handed copy of `spatial_compat_animation`, for players whose main hand is Left. A pack can replace it like any clip.

## For mod makers

- New item role `thrown_charge`: set it to true for an item your mod lets players charge and throw, or to false to keep an item out. The moment `charge_throw` is made when the throw clip starts.

# Punchy Moves v1.0.9

## Fixes
- Fixed the custom third-person camera shaking by itself when the crosshair rests on the edge of a nearby block (close-range framing no longer toggles on and off).
- Fixed punching while holding a bow freezing the legs: walking or sprinting while attacking with a bow (without shooting) made the player stand still and slide. The legs now keep the walk and sprint cycle under the punch.
- Fixed the Spatial GUI menu being placed upside down when looking up or down with the vanilla third-person camera (F5). Spatial GUI compatibility now only applies when the menu is opened from the Punchy camera; from the vanilla camera, Spatial GUI keeps its own native behavior.
- Fixed the hat layer of the skin detaching from the head in third person when another mod turns the head by itself, such as Camera Unbound's head follow: the head pointed at a random angle while the hat followed the cursor (1.20.1 and 1.21.1).
- Fixed Adaptive Skin Weathering's cold shiver making Punchy Moves give up its animations: while shivering, the walk, run and idle animations dropped back to vanilla or flickered. The shiver now plays on top of the Punchy animation.
- Fixed Create: Addictives body effects (flat, paper thin, long legs, shrinking...) making Punchy Moves give up its animations: the player dropped to the vanilla standing pose while the effect lasted. The effect now reshapes the body on top of the Punchy animation (1.20.1 and 1.21.1).
- Fixed a crash when entering a world with Cosmetica installed: both mods changed how the cape is drawn in the same spot. The cape now works with both (1.20.1 and 1.21.1).
- Fixed a constant performance cost on every client tick: the check for conflicting animation projects (Not Enough Animations, Fresh Animations: Player Extension) re-read and re-processed the name and description of every active resource pack. It now only runs again when the selected resource packs change.
- Fixed the swimming animation starting in deep water while just treading water: the model lay down horizontally while the player was still upright, out of sync with where you actually are. The swim animation now only starts once you really start swimming (sprint-swimming).
- Fixed the arms swinging much too fast while swimming: the swim stroke now follows your actual swimming speed instead of speeding up twice when sprinting.
- Fixed raising a spyglass or drawing a bow while walking throwing the arm too far: the walking arm swing (and, for the spyglass, a hidden right-click gesture) was added on top of the raised arm. The arm now stays on its aim while the body keeps walking.
- Fixed spamming left click with a spear playing an attack animation in the middle of the cooldown, sometimes an overhead swing, even though no attack happens. The spear now only animates the jabs that actually hit (1.21.11, 26.2 and 26.3).

## Changes
- The lava dive animation has been temporarily disabled. Falling into lava now uses the regular fall animation until it returns in a future update.


# Punchy! Expressions 1.0.9

## Eyes on the sides of the head

- Skins whose eyes sit on the sides of the head, as many animal skins have them, now get a face: the eyes blink, close and
  take every eye shape where they are painted.
- So do skins whose eyes reach around a corner of the head, half on the front and half on a side. Before, only the front
  half moved, or the face was read somewhere else.
- An eye on a side that has a white around its pupil glances too: the pupil slides over the white, as on the front.
- Lids, eye shapes, brows, blush, tears and the light around the eyes follow the eye around the head, and each part is lit
  as the side of the head it lies on.
- **Sides**, on the Marks tab of the face editor, puts the head's two sides beside its front, so you can mark an eye on a
  side or around a corner by hand. The grid opens on it when your skin's eyes are there.
- Export skin carries the marks on the sides too.

## Personality

- **Personality**, in the Face tab and in a new Personality tab of the face editor, picks which looks your character shows.
  Classic is every look as before. Brave is never scared: where others flinch it sets its brows. Fierce gets angry instead.
  Cute, Cheerful, Calm, Grumpy and Gloomy each have a resting face and looks of their own.
- **New from this** makes a personality of your own from any of them: pick the face it rests in, which look shows instead
  of which, or that a look does not show at all, and how pink the cheeks stay.
- **Expression strength**, from 25% to 150%, makes every look softer or stronger.
- Export skin carries your personality and the strength, so everyone with this version sees them on your avatar.

## Blush and tired eyes

- **Blush**, in the Face tab and on the Style tab: off, the cheeks never go pink.
- **Blush color**, in the Face tab and on the Colors tab.
- **Tired eyes**, in the Face tab and on the Style tab: Dark rings, Raised lids, where the lower lids come up instead, or
  Nothing.
- **Ring color**, in the Face tab and on the Colors tab.
- The face is tired less often. Standing still no longer holds heavy lids and dark rings for as long as you stand: the
  lids droop for a few seconds now and then, with no rings. The night's heavy lids and the hungry look come less often.

## Glow

- A look that paints the eyes in a color of its own, as the hearts do, now lights them in that color while it shows: the
  bloom, the glare, the trail and the tracer. With Glowing pupils on, the hearts glow too.

## Skins from skin mods

- The face now also reads a skin from a texture that a mod made itself, where before it read only the game's own skin
  textures. On Minecraft 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 it reads any such texture; from 1.21.11 on, one that loads its own picture from
  a file or a server. Mods for offline accounts bring their skins this way. It has not been tried with one of them yet: if
  your skin still gets no face, tell us which mod loads it.

# Particular Reforged 26.3

## 1.6.1

- **Update notice.** The one-time chat message about new effects now only shows in worlds that existed before the update, not in newly created ones.
- **Config.** New `enabledEffects.updateNotice` option to turn that message off.

## 1.6.0

- **Cascade foam overhaul.** Waterfall foam is now made of many small puffs instead of a few huge ones. Puffs vary in size and brightness, burst outward from the base of the fall, and grow then shrink away smoothly instead of popping.
- **Cascade mist.** A soft translucent mist now drifts off the base of waterfalls.
- **Height-based cascades.** The further the water falls, the bigger and denser the cascade. A one block drop makes a small splash of foam, a 16 block fall makes a large one.
- **Leaf snow.** Leaves with snow on top, or under falling snow, now shed clumps of snow that break into powder with small flecks drifting down. Toggle with `enabledEffects.leafSnow`, frequency in `advancedSettings.leafSnowSettings.spawnChance`.
- **Cold breath.** Players and mobs breathe out small puffs of vapour in biomes cold enough to snow. Undead, underwater and invisible creatures don't. Toggle with `enabledEffects.coldBreath`, tune in `advancedSettings.coldBreathSettings`.
- **Footstep dust.** Sprinting and landing on sand, gravel, dirt, grass and similar blocks now kicks up dust coloured after the block, replacing the vanilla sprint particles and landing burst there. The block list accepts blocks and tags in `advancedSettings.footstepDustSettings`. Toggle with `enabledEffects.footstepDust`.
- **Pollen and spores.** Flowers release drifting pollen during the day, moss and mushrooms release spores, and spores float through the air of lush caves. Toggles `enabledEffects.pollen` and `enabledEffects.spores`, frequency in `advancedSettings.pollenAndSporeSettings`.
- **Embers.** Campfires and lit furnaces throw off tiny glowing embers, blue ones for soul campfires. Toggle with `enabledEffects.embers`, tune in `advancedSettings.emberSettings`.
- **Tumbling bushes.** Dead bushes occasionally break loose and roll across dry biomes with the wind. Toggle with `enabledEffects.tumbleweeds`, tune in `advancedSettings.tumbleweedSettings`.
- **Rainbows.** After rain stops during the day a rainbow can appear opposite the sun, with a fainter secondary bow, and fade out over time. It stays in place in the distance as you move. Toggle with `enabledEffects.rainbows`, chance, duration and opacity in `advancedSettings.rainbowSettings`.
- **Screen shake.** The camera now shakes for loud nearby sounds: Warden roars and sonic booms, Ravager roars, Ender Dragon growls and explosions, fading with distance. Turn it off with `enabledEffects.screenShake`, or tune it in `advancedSettings.screenShakeSettings` with `shakeIntensity` and a `shakeSounds` list that accepts any sound ([#61](https://github.com/Leclowndu93150/Particular/issues/61)).
- **Cascade settings (config).** New `advancedSettings.cascadeSettings` section with `heightScaling`, `minIntensity`, `maxIntensity`, `maxFallHeight`, `foamDensity`, `puffSize` and `mistDensity`, plus an `enabledEffects.cascadeMist` toggle.
- **Update notice.** The first time you open each world after updating, a one-time chat message lists the new effects, in case another mod or resource pack already adds one of them.
- **API.** Other mods can now stop cascades at specific positions with `ParticularApi.addCascadeFilter((level, pos) -> ...)`. Added for Streams Reflowing compatibility ([#64](https://github.com/Leclowndu93150/Particular/issues/64)).
- **Fix.** Saved cascades and cascades being re-checked now go through the same checks as new ones, so a cascade another mod has blocked no longer comes back from the cache.
- **Fix.** Mobs and other players falling into water now make the big 3D splash reliably, sized to their fall, instead of only ripples most of the time.
- **Fix.** No longer crashes on startup with NeoForge 26.3.0.36 and newer, which removed the config type the mod was registering. Existing settings in `particular-common.toml` are kept ([#62](https://github.com/Leclowndu93150/Particular/issues/62)).

## 1.8.0

### Added
- New Quick Search UI, toggled by clicking `\` in-game
- Mod toggles are saved per profile
- Mod cards and list entries can be moved with the keyboard: focus one and press Alt+Up or Alt+Down
- Multi-select options have a Select all row
- Deleting a profile now asks you to confirm first
- The Keybinds page opens with a map of your keyboard and mouse. Hover a key to see what it does, or click it to bind something to it. Keybinds that allow it can also take Ctrl, Shift or Alt
- The keyboard map picks up your layout by itself, and you can switch between US, UK, AZERTY, QWERTZ, Dvorak and Colemak
- A list of keyboard shortcuts in the HUD editor. Open it with F1, Ctrl+/ or the button at the bottom of the editor
- Merged HUD backgrounds can blend between different colours with the new Merge with different colours option
- The HUD editor shows where the boss bar, scoreboard, action bar and titles sit, on every version including 1.8.9
- API: The UI kit has enough controls to build a whole mod screen, including select fields, split buttons, dialogs, toasts, grid reordering, progress bars and keycaps
- API: `OneConfigComposeScreen`, HUD layers, inline canvases, offscreen rendering and entity previews for drawing with Compose in your own screens and HUDs
- API: Theme tokens for state colours, typography, spacing, shapes and surfaces, and read-only player preferences such as Reduced Motion
- API: Typed config metadata keys, a tree builder with group enable toggles, self-updating dependencies, share codes and per-profile config migrations
- API: Custom pages that take an argument, typed destinations for `OneConfigUI.open` and read-only mod toggles
- API: HUD styles, borders, cloning, click regions, styled text runs and icons
- API: HUDs can hide or replace vanilla HUD elements, including the crosshair and attack indicator
- API: Attack, place block, player turn and block update events
- API: Keybinds can stay out of Minecraft's controls screen
- API: Notification handles, a warning type and theme colours for notifications
- API: Segmented and pill tabs can slide a pill between options

### Changed
- Every OneConfig screen now uses the same controls, so buttons, menus, fields and tooltips look and behave the same everywhere
- Menus open from the control you clicked, follow the theme's shape and panels, and give keyboard focus back when they close
- Tooltips wait 300 ms before they show
- A disabled option now dims its label and control instead of greying out the whole card
- Number fields drop trailing zeros, so 0.50 shows as 0.5
- Scrolling glides in lists added by mods
- The HUD editor's selection box follows your theme's accent colour
- The HUD editor tells you why two HUDs won't merge. To pull a HUD out of a merged group, hold Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) while dragging it or use its right-click menu

- Mod Menu opens OneConfig mod settings faster

- OneConfig asks the GPU for its state less often while drawing
- The colour picker opens lined up with the end of its button
- Options without a title no longer show a placeholder label
- Mod toggles and card types update on every screen at once

### Fixed
- Fixed undo / redo changing all actions taken during a session
- Fixed the keyboard focus ring never showing in the Minecraft themes
- Colours stored inside a config object now load their saved value instead of the default
- The resource reload event no longer fires a second time for server datapack reloads
- Text in the Minecraft font lines up with the pixel grid again instead of bleeding into the next pixel

# Wavify 1.5.0

@Mod Updates I have secretly been working on more stuff for wavify, and i believe its kind of ready now!

## New: Effects
A new **Effects** config section

- **Boat wakes** – V-shaped foam trails behind moving boats with spray at the bow. 
- **Entity ripples** – ripple rings around players and mobs wading, swimming or landing in water.
- **Waterfall mist** – mist, spray and foam rings where falling water lands.
- **Rain ripples** – little rings on the water surface while it rains.
- **Ice & slush** – waves fade out when they reach ice, slush on freezing oceans.

Each one can be toggled on its own.

### New: River wave styles
New **River Wave Style** option:

- **Crest** – curved crests (the old look)
- **Streaks** – thin foam lines along the current
- **Swell** – soft, wide bands
- **Rapids** – choppy whitewater
- **Auto** – picks a style per spot based on river width and depth

### New: Weather
- Rain and thunderstorms now make bigger, faster and more frequent waves. Controlled with **Weather Intensity** (0 turns it off).
- Wet sand now dries out gradually after a wave pulls back. Set the time with **Wet Sand Dry Time** (in ticks, 0 = instant).

### New: Quality & performance
- **Quality** preset: Performance, Balanced, Fancy, Ultra. Sets render radius, river wave radius/density and effects amount in one click.
- **Auto Performance** (on by default): when your FPS drops and Wavify is part of the reason, it spawns fewer waves and effects until things recover.

### Shaders
- **Auto Shader Offsets** (on by default): uses a tested wave height offset for Complementary, BSL, Sildur's, MakeUp, Bliss, Photon, Solas and Rethinking Voxels. Other packs still use Shader Wave Y Sink.

### River waves
- Waves now fade out while they're still moving instead of stopping and fading in place.
- Each wave wobbles and curls slightly on top of the current, so they don't all move in lockstep.
- Waves live longer and vary more in length, and spawn in a steady trickle instead of in batches.
- Hitting a bank makes a wave slow down and coast instead of stopping dead.
- Default **River Wave Travel Blocks** raised from 11 to 18 (max raised from 32 to 48).

### Compatibility
- Modded rivers and oceans are now recognized through the common `c:is_river` / `c:is_ocean` biome tags.
- **Biome Color Overrides** now accept biome tags, e.g. `#c:is_cold=3D57D6`. Exact biome ids still win over tags.

updates.name: dynamicsurroundingsfabric
updates.changelog:
**AI Disclosure**
* Built the world actors and the firefly bush fireflies, and measured each with benchmark runs
* Wrote tests that feed the mod's configuration broken values, which found sound settings that gave broken pitches, and fixed them
* Found a fog jump with mods that draw distant terrain by running one alongside the mod, and fixed it on this side
* Traced the sources of the mod's sounds, and cut, cleaned and leveled the replacements chosen by ear

**What's New**
* World actors are things that move through the world on their own. Every player in a world sees the same ones in the same places, because each one's path comes from the world's seed
  * Dust devils cross deserts, badlands and savannas on clear days. Each is a swaying funnel of dust in the color of the ground that lifts sand and dry plants, and water or a wall breaks it up
  * Waterspouts reach from the sea to the clouds over oceans that aren't cold, more often in a storm. They throw up spray at their foot and tear seagrass and kelp from shallow water, and they break up when they come ashore or reach ice
  * Snowspouts whirl powder snow over snowy plains and frozen lakes on clear days
  * Firespouts whirl tongues of flame up from the Nether's lava lakes, with smoke, sparks and a roar of fire, and light up what is around them
  * Wisps are pale lights that drift low over marshes and swamps at night. They go out as you come near and show again farther off. Turquoise soul-fire wisps haunt soul sand valleys
  * Apparitions are pale, see-through figures in a villager's shape that fade away below the waist. Each is dressed as a villager of its biome, in any profession (a farmer's hat, a librarian's)
    * They glide between their haunts in dark forests and pale gardens at night, now and then in a swamp, and in the Nether's soul sand valleys, finding their way around trees and walls
    * One turns its head to watch you and fades away as you come near, to show again farther off
    * They sometimes come in twos or threes, and three times as often in the week either side of Halloween
    * They're under Scary Content, and set by the RPG preset rather than Atmosphere
  * World actors are on by default, with a switch for each kind in World Actor Options. The Atmosphere and Defaults presets also set them, and the Vanilla+ preset turns them off. `/dsactor` summons one ahead of you
  * Modpacks can give them to biomes with `actors` in `biomes.json`, and to dimensions with `worldActors` in `dimensions.json`
* Firefly bushes give off the mod's fireflies in place of the game's, winking with a halo and a light. They're under Fireflies in Firefly Options
* Each sound in the individual sound configuration has a reset button. It puts the sound's action and volume back to what they were when the screen was opened. With Ctrl held, it puts them back to the mod's defaults instead, such as culled farm animals and the game's water sound blocked for the waterfalls
* `/dsconflicts` lists the effects a shader pack keeps off, among those switched on in the configuration
* Modpacks can name constants and functions in `dsconfigs/scripts.json` and use them in any script as `def.NAME` and `def.name()`, such as `def.isHalloween()`
  * A function is either for biome rules (traits such as `SPOOKY`) or for everything else (`diurnal.isNight()` and the like), and functions may use one another
  * Definitions are checked as they load, and a mistyped name or a loop is reported with the file it's in
  * A later file's definition replaces ours, but nothing defined in the mod's code can be replaced
* Modpacks can give a biome loop in `biomes.json` a `volume` script (0 to 1) so the loop follows the player, such as `math.sqrt(lib.smoothStep(-4, 4, player.getY()))` to bring a sound in by height. The new `lib.smoothStep(from, to, x)` is for blends like this

**Sounds**
* Replaced: calm rain, heartbeat, wolf howls, whale song (humpback), loon, seagulls, owl, nightingale, eagle, player jump, the hotbar's equip click, electric arc, dust storm, the forest, deep forest and jungle loops, deep forest crickets, the cave drone underground, the biggest waterfalls, and the waterspout
* Cleaned: the silent forest loop
* Added: a medium rain between the calm rain and the game's downpour, right whale and minke whale calls, a seagull flock, more red-shouldered hawk calls, loops for sparse forests and for sparse and swampy jungles, and a deeper drone below y 0 that blends with the cave drone
* Removed: the red-tailed hawk, and sounds nothing played (insect crawl, Nether and End ambience, water drops)
* Wolves, whales, loons, seagulls, owls, nightingales and the hotbar click vary in pitch as they play
* Every sound is credited in `CREDITS.md`, and every one allows commercial use

**Changes**
* The mod's fireflies are drawn as the game's firefly in place of the end rod's sparkle. The dot stays visible between flashes and takes on the light's color as it flashes. A resource pack's firefly texture is used
* Fair weather clouds are no longer flat slabs from below. A cloud's thin edge is tucked up a step, and the middle of a tall one hangs a step lower
* Ground fog lies under huge mushrooms and Biomes O' Plenty's giant flowers, as it does under trees, rather than on top of them with streaks of mist hanging from their edges. Modpacks can add other mods' canopies to the `dsurround:effects/fog_canopy` block tag
* Beach waves and mud footprints follow the storm strength `/dsweather` holds
* `/dsmm whatsplaying` names the game's music tracks the way the game's "now playing" message does, such as "C418 - Sweden", in your language
* Modded tools and weapons get their equip and swing sounds without being tagged. An item that no tag names is known by what it does, such as being drawn like a bow or raised like a shield, what its tool mines, or whether it's a weapon. On NeoForge, modded fishing rods, maces and spears tagged the convention way are now found
* Pickaxes have an item class of their own, which sounds like the axes' for now
* More blocks have effects. New 26.3 plants rustle and crunch underfoot, wool slabs and leaf litter soak up rain, and blocks from Biomes O' Plenty, BetterEnd, BetterNether, Ecologics, Promenade, Terrestria, Wilder Wild and Enderscape are covered
* Frames in heavy rain are up to a quarter shorter. While the mod's particle weather replaces the game's rain and snow, the game no longer works out its own weather for drawing, which took up to a quarter of the render thread in a heavy storm (more with Serene Seasons)
* The lights that fireflies and flame jets cast are drawn all at once, which takes less than half the GPU time in a field of fireflies. Ground fog takes 11-15% less
* Dynamic clouds take a fifth to a third less of each tick. Far clouds, past about the render distance, change shape less often, and the biome under a cloud is read more cheaply
* Enhanced sounds take about half the work to trace through open air
* On NeoForge, the mod reads other mods' files through NeoForge rather than opening each mod's jar and keeping it open, which took 36 MB of memory in a pack of 120 mods

**Fixes**
* With a mod that draws terrain past the render distance, fog from dust storms, biomes and mornings now closes in smoothly from the far horizon. Before, a dust storm at a quarter of its strength made the view jump from the horizon to about 230 blocks
* With dynamic clouds on, sheet lightning was all but invisible through a storm's fog. It now lights the clouds through the fog
* Once a thunderstorm's thunder ends, the rain left behind only eases off, so the clouds no longer close over and darken again part way through clearing
* A volume or pitch in a sound configuration that the mod can't use, such as `-1e400`, is reported as an error instead of giving the sound a broken pitch
* Rings from something falling into water no longer hang inside a waterfall or float on flowing water
* Beach wave foam lies at random angles instead of all facing one way
* Boat wake foam follows Bobbing Rings instead of the waterfall Froth setting
* Clouds, lightning and particle weather fall back to the game's when another mod keeps the mod from drawing them, instead of disappearing
* A modded effect that can't make its particles no longer breaks the target portrait
* A failure in the waterfall mist shader no longer takes away what soft flames, point lights, ground fog and dust need to draw properly
* With a shader pack, a strike that fails to draw no longer garbles the game's own lightning
* Fixed a crash with Music and Melody while one of its tracks played and a mod (Simple Music Control) asked what was playing (#215)
